worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/54727a51e88b3543726b61606a0f41b9a8cf5ec46ef4c69d7233fd54a4b50242.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x)$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=x\,⟹\,x=y.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le y\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14163455/assets/956aaf81973d9a2b3e56082ecae8e654eee55d6f99c42dd433d126632d7c7262.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{x}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{4}}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{2}{e}^{{y}^{4}}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{{y}^{4}}[{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{2}\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{{y}^{4}}}{3}[{x}^{3}]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{3}\,{e}^{{y}^{4}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{[{e}^{{y}^{4}}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$
